1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned A.G.A. who appears on behalf of the State Respondents and Sri Shailendra Kumar Tiwari, Advocate who has filed his vakalatnama on behalf of the opposite party no. 3, which is taken on record.

2. This petition has been filed with the following main prayers:-
"A. Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Certiorari thereby quashing the Impugned First Information Report (lodged by Opposite Party No. 3) dated 17.08.2023, FIR. No.-0416 of 2023, Case Crime No. 0416 of 2023, Under Section Ranjeet Tiwari vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

entities.text: Section Ranjeet Tiwari vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182552474/
1 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Vibhuti Khand, District - Lucknow, with respect to the Petitioner in the light of Compromise dated 10 10 2023 entered into between the informant and the petitioner, as contained in ANNEXURE NO. 1 to this Writ Petition.
B. Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the Opposite Party No. 2 to not to arrest or adopt any coercive measures against the Petitioner on the basis of Impugned First Information Report dated 17.08.2023."
3. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the dispute is monetary in nature and both the parties are entered into a compromise.
4. The respondent no. 3 has given an affidavit that he wishes not to pursue the matter any further and he also not disputed such contention of compromise.

5. The writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the petitioner and the private respondent to approach the Investigating officer concerned alongwith their alleged compromise who shall verify the same and take an appropriate decision strictly in accordance with law, thereafter, within a period of three weeks.
6. The Registry is directed to return the original compromise annexed in the writ petition after retaining a photocopy of the same to the petitioner.
